absent: Internal allocation, locking, and address space management of the shared caller-aware mapping helper and the encrypted mapping helper.
Numeric encodings of cache modes and protection conversion rules plus caller address tracking use.
Contracts of persistent region detection, firmware type and attribute queries, table address checks, and firmware memory classification.
Locking, sleeping, and concurrency rules for remap, unmap, early mapping, and shadow population helpers and flush scope.
Values of page table masks, fixed map indices, shadow range bounds, kernel image boundaries, and allocation failure handling beyond stated warnings.
Entropy source quality, enablement predicate internals, initial base values, and interaction with device memory and hotplug.
Probe registration, fault dispatch, arming and disarming sequence, deferred release timing, and per-CPU nesting protocol.

findings.text: Four mapping helpers expose distinct caching behaviors for a physical range and length. Three request write combining, write through, and write back attributes respectively, while the fourth derives its caching attribute from a supplied protection value. Each forwards to a shared caller-aware helper together with the caller return address and a non-exclusive request flag.
A write back remapping choice returns a cached mapping when the caller asks for decrypted access or when the platform uses host memory encryption, and otherwise returns an encrypted mapping.

Device address translation maps the single page containing the requested physical address with write back semantics, adds the intra-page offset to the result on success and returns null on failure. The companion release helper unmaps the containing page derived from the previously returned address.

Decrypted mapping is required for any overlap with persistent memory, for reserved firmware areas carrying a nonvolatile attribute when firmware boot is active, and for persistent RAM. Reserved and firmware-related table types also require decrypted mapping except under guest memory encryption where they remain encrypted.

Firmware data detection is false unless firmware boot is active. When active it reports true if the address equals the stored memory map address or system table address reconstructed from high and low halves, if it is a known table address, or if its memory type denotes boot services data or runtime services data.

Setup data inspection walks the boot chain starting from the boot parameter link. For each entry it reports true on exact address match or when the query falls inside the header plus payload extent, follows indirect entries through their secondary address and length, releases each temporary mapping before advancing, and ends false at chain termination. Early and late wrappers select decrypted early mapping versus normal mapping with combined flags.

RAM remapping is always allowed without memory encryption. With encryption an explicitly encrypted request is allowed and an explicitly decrypted request is denied. Under host encryption, setup data and firmware data addresses are denied. All other addresses use the negation of the decrypted-mapping predicate.

Early protection adjustment leaves protection unchanged without memory encryption. With encryption it starts from an encrypted assumption, clears it for setup or firmware data under host encryption, clears it when the decrypted-mapping predicate holds, and then converts through the encrypted or decrypted protection helper accordingly.
Physical memory encryption query delegates to the RAM remap permission check with no additional request flags for the given address and length.

Boot fixed mapping uses a single page aligned table of page entries sized to fill one page, cleared during early initialization and populated into the kernel address space for the boot mapping window.

Early fixed mapping support resolves the middle directory from the currently loaded top table rather than assuming the swapper table, indexes the boot entry table by virtual address, tests whether a pointer lies inside that table, initializes the table and installs it for the boot window, and installs or clears an individual fixed mapping followed by a single entry flush.

The boot mapping window must reside within a single middle directory and the fixed zero conversion plus one page must preserve middle directory alignment. Protection values are masked against the supported mask before installation, a zero value clears rather than installs, and every install or clear flushes the affected kernel virtual address.

Setup chain inspection warns and returns a negative answer when a temporary mapping fails, including the indirect entry second mapping. Early mapping initialization warns when the boot window spans middle directories and emits diagnostic details, and the fixed mapping installer stops the system on an out of range index.

Early sanitizer shadow setup fills per-level early tables from physical addresses of the next level with kernel table and encryption attributes masked to the supported set, installs early shadow coverage into both early and initial top tables, clears shadow directory ranges with distinct handling for five level versus folded four level configurations, and shallowly allocates missing upper levels on demand.

Full sanitizer initialization copies the initial top table to the early table, isolates the colliding trailing entry under five level paging through a temporary table, switches address spaces with full flushes, clears and repopulates shadow coverage for direct map gaps, recorded physical ranges, allocation space with distinct full virtual mode handling, shared entry area, kernel image, and module tail, then restores the initial table, clears and write protects the early shadow page with a final flush, resets the initial task depth, and runs generic initialization.

Randomization describes each movable region with pointers to its base and optional end plus a size measured in terabytes. The initial table holds three entries for the direct map with an end pointer, the dynamic allocation area, and the frame map, with sizes filled during randomization.

Each region padding equals its terabyte size shifted to bytes. Direct map sizing starts from the maximum physical bits, then shrinks to observed memory plus configured padding unless device private zones are enabled, while the frame map size derives from the direct map size scaled by per-frame descriptor size and rounded up to terabytes.

Memory randomization validates layout ordering against the entry area and kernel map, presets the direct map end to the maximum physical value, seeds a deterministic generator, distributes remaining entropy across regions with directory-aligned random offsets, assigns each base, updates the direct map end from the placed direct region, and advances with minimum alignment padding.

Tracing support tracks faulting pages with list linkage, deferred release linkage, requested address, prior presence value, armed flag, registration count, and scheduled release flag. Deferred release batches pages through a callback head, and per-CPU context records the active fault page, probe, saved flags, address, and nesting depth.

A single architecture spin lock guards linkage of fault pages into a small hashed table while the registration count is owned by writers under read copy update discipline and consumed by the post handler. A global unsigned counter tracks active instrumentation and per-CPU context holds the currently handled fault with no additional locking stated.
Terabyte shift has decimal value forty and defines conversion between terabyte counts and byte sizes for padding and region sizing.
Randomization address ceiling equals the CPU entry area base. The direct map physical end is an unsigned long that becomes read only after initialization.
Instrumentation hash uses four bits yielding sixteen table buckets each a list head. The active count is an unsigned integer and per-CPU context storage is defined for the context descriptor.
Sanitizer log formatting prepends the sanitizer name followed by colon and space to each message, and the early five level table selector is defined as an empty marker.
Temporary fixed address top used for boot range span checking equals the negation of one page size.
